Apply and check background knowledge

Source: R/knowledge.R
orient.Rd

orient() returns the tightest graph that agrees with both cg and bk: an MPDAG, or a DAG if every edge is directed. It errors with class caugi_inconsistent if no DAG agrees with both.

holds() checks each statement of edges(bk, expand = TRUE): TRUE if it holds in every DAG cg stands for, FALSE if in none, and NA otherwise.

Usage

orient(cg, bk)

holds(cg, bk)

Arguments

cg

A caugi with only --> and --- edges, such as a DAG, PDAG, CPDAG or MPDAG.

bk

Background knowledge, made by knowledge().

Value

orient(): a caugi. holds(): edges(bk, expand = TRUE) with a logical column holds.

References

E. Perkovic, M. Kalisch and M. H. Maathuis (2017). Interpreting and using CPDAGs with background knowledge. In Proceedings of the 33rd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI-17).

See also

Other knowledge: is_knowledge(), knowledge(), required(), set_tiers(), tiers()

Examples

cpdag <- caugi(A %---% B, B %---% C, class = "CPDAG")
bk <- knowledge(A %-->% B)
holds(cpdag, bk) # NA: some DAGs have A --> B, some B --> A
orient(cpdag, bk) # A --> B --> C
#> <caugi object; 3 nodes, 2 edges; simple: TRUE; session=0x5b62049f8140>
#>   graph_class: DAG
#>   nodes: A, B, C
#>   edges: A-->B, B-->C
